title: Arithmetic and assignment: quotient, remainder, and safe intermediates
goal: Separate computing a value from storing it in a variable.

prerequisites.text: You know initialization and the difference between an expression and a statement.

sections.title: From the task to an operation
paragraphs: In sum = sum + 3, read the old sum, add 3, then store the new value back. For this integer variable, sum += 3 is a shorthand for the same operation. sum + 3 alone does not store the result.

For integers, 17/5 is 3 and 17%5 is 2: 3×5+2=17. Division by zero is invalid. For negative operands, division truncates toward zero; this first example uses nonnegative numbers. For large calculations, check type bounds, including intermediate products.

sections.title: When the result differs
paragraphs: sum=+2 assigns positive 2; it does not add 2. The order of the += symbols matters.

sections.title: Now solve your own task
paragraphs: Start with balance=20; add 7, then subtract 5. Print balance and explain both assignments.

terms.definition: The result of integer / with the fractional part discarded toward zero.
For valid integer division, related to the quotient by a = (a / b) * b + a % b.
